definition: Artificial consciousness, also known as machine consciousness, synthetic consciousness, or digital consciousness, is consciousness hypothesized to be possible for artificial intelligence.
details: It is also the corresponding field of study, which draws insights from philosophy of mind, philosophy of artificial intelligence, cognitive science and neuroscience. The term "sentience" can be used when specifically designating ethical considerations stemming from a form of phenomenal consciousness (P-consciousness, or the ability to feel qualia). Since sentience involves the ability to experience ethically positive or negative (i.e., valenced) mental states, it may justify welfare concerns and legal protection, as with non-human animals. Some scholars believe that consciousness is generated by the interoperation of various parts of the brain; these mechanisms are labeled the neural correlates of consciousness (NCC). Some further believe that constructing a system (e.g., a computer system) that can emulate this NCC interoperation would result in a system that is conscious. Some scholars reject the possibility of non-biological conscious beings.

explainer.lead: Artificial consciousness asks whether an artificial intelligence could actually have conscious experiences, rather than merely behave as if it did. The question matters because a system capable of positive or negative experiences could raise concerns about its welfare and legal protection.

tiers.eli5: Imagine building a robot that can talk about feeling happy or sad. Artificial consciousness is the question of whether it could really have those feelings, or whether it would only be acting like it does. Some people think copying the way parts of the brain work together could make this possible, while others think only living brains can be conscious.
tiers.practitioner: For engineers, this is primarily a research question rather than an established capability to implement. One proposed approach is to construct a computer system that emulates the interoperation of neural correlates of consciousness, but whether that would produce consciousness remains disputed. A system's reports or convincing behavior should not by itself be treated as evidence of felt experience.
tiers.paperLevel: Artificial consciousness is hypothesized consciousness in artificial intelligence, and also names the corresponding interdisciplinary field of study. A central proposal is that if consciousness arises from the interoperation of neural correlates of consciousness (NCC), emulating that interoperation in a computer system might yield consciousness. Its possibility is contested, including by scholars who reject non-biological conscious beings; sentience specifically concerns valenced phenomenal experience and associated ethical considerations.

explainer.example: Suppose researchers build a computer system whose interacting components emulate mechanisms identified as neural correlates of consciousness. On the NCC-based view, that system might become conscious; critics could still deny that such emulation creates experience.

usedIn.name: Philosophy of mind
usedIn.detail: Examines what consciousness is and whether it could exist in an artificial system.

usedIn.name: Philosophy of artificial intelligence
usedIn.detail: Investigates the possibility and implications of conscious AI.

usedIn.name: Cognitive science
usedIn.detail: Contributes accounts of mental processes relevant to artificial consciousness.

usedIn.name: Neuroscience
usedIn.detail: Studies brain mechanisms, including proposed neural correlates of consciousness.

explainer.intuition: There is a difference between producing behavior associated with consciousness and actually having an inner experience. Artificial consciousness concerns whether an artificial system could have the latter.
howItWorks: Start with the hypothesis that consciousness can arise in an artificial system.
Identify interacting brain mechanisms proposed as neural correlates of consciousness.
Construct a computer system that emulates their interoperation.
Ask whether that emulation would produce consciousness, a claim scholars dispute.
explainer.whyItMatters: If an artificial system were sentient and could experience ethically positive or negative states, its welfare could become a moral concern. Such experiences might also support arguments for legal protection, analogous to those made for non-human animals.
misconceptions: Artificial consciousness is not simply intelligence or humanlike behavior.
Sentience specifically concerns felt, valenced experience, not consciousness in every sense.
The NCC-based proposal is a hypothesis, not an agreed method for creating consciousness.
